item.title: CVE-2026-99804 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference
io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free read in this path.
Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99800 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring: free the task context after a grace period
A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work() running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else branch:
percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1); if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel))) wake_up(&tctx->wait); put_task_struct(tctx->task);
The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(), and on exec it frees the tctx right after. Nothing holds that off for the remaining three lines, the task reference only covers a tctx freed along with the task_struct. It used to work out because io_uring_del_tctx_node() took the uring_lock that the freeing side holds across io_put_task(), until that moved to tctx_lock.
Free the tctx with kfree_rcu(), and enter an RCU read section in io_put_task() before the count is dropped.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99798 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work
An IOPOLL ring without DEFER_TASKRUN can be reaped by a task other than the one that submitted the I/O. If a polled request is marked REQ_F_REISSUE, io_free_batch_list() calls io_queue_iowq() with the original tctx. Ordinary task exit can tear down tctx->io_wq after draining only the tracked requests. The live request pins the task, but not its io-wq, so the foreign task can race io_wq_put_and_exit() and enqueue through a freed or NULL queue.
Forward foreign userspace enqueues to the owning task before accessing tctx->io_wq. Use a dedicated task_work callback so reissues still go straight to io-wq, and fail them if task_work is running in cancellation mode. Preserve the existing PF_KTHREAD cancellation path. This also covers the other callers of io_queue_iowq() without changing the worker-owned enqueue path.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99794 [CVSS:3.1 8.3 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states
A peer can send configuration messages while an incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the security or deferred accept gate has completed. A configuration response can then promote the channel to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also act on channels that are closing, and a late connection response can move a disconnecting channel back to BT_CONFIG.
Accept connection responses only while waiting in BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete configuration in BT_CONFIG.
Score: 8.3 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L

item.title: CVE-2026-99793 [CVSS:3.1 8.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests
An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then sends its connection request. A peer can answer it before that with a connection response matching our source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG, completes configuration and becomes connected before security has completed. If security then fails, l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach the required security level.
A connection response with a zero source CID is matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the same identifier for a response it still has to send, so the lookup can pick the wrong channel.
Only accept a connection response while our request is outstanding, and only look at such channels when matching by identifier.
Score: 8.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

item.title: CVE-2026-99792 [CVSS:3.1 8.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect
TREE_DISCONNECT closes the tree's published file handles before marking and removing the tree connection. A concurrent CREATE that already holds a tree reference can therefore publish its file after the close pass. When CREATE drops its reference, the tree can be freed while the published file still points to it.
Mark and remove the tree connection before closing its files, and serialize both new-open and durable-reconnect volatile ID publication with that state transition. An opener is then either published in time for the close pass or rejected after disconnect with STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED.
Keep a tree reference while a file carries its tree pointer. This protects asynchronous users that can defer the file's final destruction past tree disconnect.
The close pass can race the successful FP_NEW to FP_INITED transition. Take the opening request's file reference atomically with that transition. This keeps the file alive until request completion even if teardown removes the ID immediately.
BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in proc_show_files (fs/smb/server/vfs_cache.c:126) Read of size 4 at addr ff11000101540f80 by task poc/153
Call Trace: proc_show_files (fs/smb/server/vfs_cache.c:126) seq_read_iter (fs/seq_file.c:231) proc_reg_read_iter (fs/proc/inode.c:299) vfs_read (fs/read_write.c:574) ksys_read (fs/read_write.c:716) do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84) entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121)
Allocated by: ksmbd_tree_conn_connect (fs/smb/server/mgmt/tree_connect.c:35) smb2_tree_connect (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:2819) handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:368)
Freed by: kfree (mm/slub.c:6801) handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:332)
Score: 8.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99785 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe
p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to 65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE attribute buffer.
Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag, which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a seq_file implementation detail.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99773 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind
In [1], sashiko reported the following issue:
=== snip === Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence() creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC.
The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops (like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via synchronize_rcu().
If userspace calls ioctl(SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO) concurrently with a device hot-unplug:
CPU1 (Userspace) sync_file_get_name() ops = rcu_dereference(fence->ops); if (!dma_fence_test_signaled_flag()) // Preempted or delayed here
CPU2 (Driver Teardown) Signals the fence (setting fence->ops = NULL) Destroys and frees the CRTC without waiting for an RCU grace period
CPU1 (Resumes) ops->get_driver_name(fence) -> drm_crtc_fence_get_driver_name() crtc = fence_to_crtc(fence); // Casts to the freed CRTC return crtc->dev->driver->name; // Use-after-free
...
Does the CRTC or DRM device need to be kept alive for the RCU grace period, or should the fence hold a proper reference to prevent the use-after-free when get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() access the freed CRTC structure? === snap ===
I believe this to be a correct observation and this patch implements the suggestion of waiting for an RCU grace period before proceeding with destruction of the drm_crtc, so that get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() can still work.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99761 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT
batadv_mesh_free() releases the translation tables via batadv_tt_free() before batadv_originator_free() stops orig_work. The purge worker can therefore still run while the TT is torn down. When an originator times out, batadv_purge_orig_ref() calls batadv_tt_global_del_orig(), which loads tt.global_hash and walks all buckets while taking their locks:
CPU0 CPU1 batadv_tt_free() batadv_purge_orig() batadv_tt_global_del_orig() hash = ...tt.global_hash; batadv_tt_global_table_free() batadv_hash_destroy(hash); spin_lock_bh(&hash->list_locks[i]);
Disable orig_work at the beginning of batadv_mesh_free(), directly after the mesh was marked as deactivating. The second disable_delayed_work_sync() in batadv_originator_free() is harmless because it is free'd anyway.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99760 [CVSS:3.1 7.6 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes
A received TT change (OGM diff or full table response) with the ROAM flag but without DEL is handled by batadv_tt_global_add() like a ROAMING_ADV:
* a newly created global entry gets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM and is therefore excluded from the global CRC. The sender has it in its local CRC and the receiver has to request the full table again * batadv_tt_global_purge_local() removes the local entry of the receiver. The receiver's own client is considered as roamed to the sender and frames for it are rerouted
The ROAM flag only has a meaning together with DEL. Drop it on reception to keep it from populating the global table with a temporary ROAMING entry which is not part of the CRC - and therefore causing a CRC mismatch.
Score: 7.6 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99758 [CVSS:3.1 7.5 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()
sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3 bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.
Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.
Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.
Score: 7.5 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99754 [CVSS:3.1 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated
iscsi_parse_pr_out_transport_id() returns the ISID of a FORMAT CODE 01b TransportID as a pointer into the PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT parameter list, lowercased in place and never null-terminated. spc4r37 Table 508 requires the field to be null-terminated, but a non-conforming initiator can omit the NULL; when the ISID ends at the end of the received buffer, the pointer is not a C string.
The registration code still consumes it as one: strcmp() in __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg() and in the REGISTER AND MOVE path, and snprintf("%s") in __core_scsi3_do_alloc_registration(), which also reads its first 8 bytes unconditionally with get_unaligned_be64() - a NUL check does not bound that read.
When the parameter list spans more than one page, transport_kmap_data_sg() maps it with vmap(), and the over-read walks off the end of the mapping into the vmalloc() guard page and oopses. Reproduced with a PR OUT REGISTER + SPEC_I_PT parameter list of exactly 8192 bytes whose final TransportID carries a 12-byte ISID without a terminating NUL:
BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffc9000138c000 RIP: 0010:strcmp+0xc/0x30 Call Trace: __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg+0xd3/0x120 [target_core_mod] core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port+0x8fc/0x13a0 [target_core_mod] core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register+0x73c/0x900 [target_core_mod] ... iscsi_target_rx_thread+0xef/0x1d0 [iscsi_target_mod]
With a single-page parameter list the buffer is a kmap() direct mapping, so the over-read continues into the physically adjacent page instead of faulting. snprintf("%s") then copies whatever follows the ISID in memory into pr_reg_isid, and PR IN READ FULL STATUS reports the registration back to any initiator, turning the over-read into an info leak of kernel heap contents. Reproduced with a 4096-byte parameter list whose last TransportID ends at the end of the buffer with a 4-byte ISID and no NUL, interleaved with I/O to populate adjacent pages: the READ FULL STATUS response returned the ISID as "0xleak" followed by raw bytes that were not part of the parameter list. The snprintf() into pr_reg_isid[PR_REG_ISID_LEN] caps the echoed ISID at 15 characters, so at most 11 bytes past the buffer are leaked per command, but the PR OUT command is not rate limited.
Any initiator that can send PR OUT to an iSCSI-exported LUN can trigger either variant, including a guest via vhost-scsi.
Require 8 bytes to remain after the ",i,0x" separator, and a NUL inside the rest of the descriptor, before the ISID pointer is returned. REGISTER AND MOVE fails with TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST; on SPEC_I_PT no target port claims the malformed TransportID, and the command fails the same way.
Score: 7.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99753 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure
If ttm_bo_init_validate() fails, it drops the buffer object's reference and cleans it up through the supplied destroy callback. lsdc_bo_destroy() releases the GEM object and frees the enclosing lsdc_bo, so freeing it again in lsdc_bo_create() causes a double free on a synchronous failure path.
Let TTM own the cleanup after initialization has started and return the error directly. Keep the explicit free on drm_gem_object_init() failure, which occurs before ownership is passed to TTM.
Tested on LS7A2000 by making drm_vma_offset_add() return -ENOSPC for one selected dumb-buffer creation. The error reached userspace, the destroy callback ran once, and no handle was published or tracked BO retained. Normal buffer creation, zeroing, mapping, readback and release passed.
AI assistance was used for the ownership analysis, fix, fault-injection tools, build and test execution.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99746 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ASoC: SOF: Intel: hda-sdw-bpt: Stop active DMA before closing BPT streams
When sdw_enable_stream() fails in intel_ace2x_bpt_send_async() after hda_sdw_bpt_send_async() has already started the TX and RX DMA streams, intel_ace2x_bpt_close_stream() invokes hda_sdw_bpt_close() directly without calling hda_sdw_bpt_wait(). As a result, hda_sdw_bpt_dma_deprepare() tears down the DMA buffers and BDL while the DMA hardware is still running.
Disable any running TX or RX BPT DMA stream at the start of hda_sdw_bpt_close() before unmapping channels and depreparing DMA resources.
Score: 7 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99744 [CVSS:3.1 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
net: atl1c: drop oversized RX frames instead of panicking
atl1c sizes its receive buffers from the netdev MTU plus a fixed set of L2 overheads, which comes to 1522 bytes at the default MTU. A link partner that sends a longer frame - in practice a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe, whose RouterOS side defaults to l2mtu 1600 while the host stays at MTU 1500 - makes the length reported by the RX return descriptor exceed what the hardware wrote, and skb_put() then either includes bytes that were never received or trips skb_over_panic and takes the host down.
Compare the descriptor length against buffer_info->length, the length the hardware was given, rather than against skb_tailroom(): the skb carries 64 bytes of slack for the DMA erratum, so tailroom is larger than the DMA buffer and a frame in between would pass the check and still be delivered with a tail the device never wrote. The same test rejects frames shorter than ETH_HLEN + ETH_FCS_LEN; before this change a reported length below ETH_FCS_LEN underflowed in skb_put().
The frame is dropped with kfree_skb_reason(SKB_DROP_REASON_PKT_TOO_BIG) so drop_monitor and the kfree_skb tracepoint see it, and counted through dev_core_stats_rx_dropped_inc(), which survives atl1c_get_stats() overwriting the hardware counters on every read. It also counts as work: atl1c_clean_rfd() has already recycled the RFD, and the refill at the end of the poll only runs when work_done is non-zero, so sustained oversized traffic would otherwise drain the ring and stop RX.
Tested on a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe (4x AR8151) in a Proxmox VE host, with atl1c built from a DKMS tree carrying this change: the l2mtu-1600 traffic that panics the stock driver is dropped and counted with the patch applied, and received normally once the host MTU is raised to match.
This complements commit 36c2009d90f2 ("net: atl1c: fix soft lockup on out-of-range tpd_cons read"), which fixed the TX side of the same "host dies while the card resets" problem.
Score: 7.1 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99735 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables
MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table entries in walk_pud_range() and walk_pmd_range() when walking to the next level. These copies can become stale when khugepaged or MADV_DONTNEED (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM) removes a PTE table concurrently.
This pattern dates back to commit bd74fdaea146 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: support page table walks"). Likely, earlier locking masked the latent bug. Later changes exposed it: commit 1d65b771bc08 ("mm/khugepaged: retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock") allowed concurrent retraction, and commit cf4a65539c13 ("memcg-v1: no need for memcg locking for MGLRU") dropped the walker's outer RCU protection.
The fix is simple, so just fix the original commit so we don't have to speculate. To fix it, pass the actual PMD/PUD pointers. This restores the RCU-protected lookup and validation against the live PMD. Note that the PUD handling is required as well to handle folded page tables correctly in all cases.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
[ david: handle walk_pud_range() as well, clarify+simplify description, adjust Fixes: ]
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99730 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock
On a retried fault, a fatal signal interrupting the folio lock wait makes lock_folio_maybe_drop_mmap() drop the fault lock without pinning the file. However, filemap_fault() may still need to release mapping->invalidate_lock. A concurrent munmap() can release the last file reference and free the mapping before that unlock.
Defer dropping the fault lock to filemap_fault()'s retry cleanup, after releasing invalidate_lock. If the fault lock was already dropped for I/O, release the existing file reference instead. Keep the fault lock held for FAULT_FLAG_RETRY_NOWAIT as before.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99728 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/huge_memory: fix list corruption when deferred_split_scan() races with deferred_split_folio()
Since the deferred split queue became a list_lru, the isolate callback moves the folios it took a reference on to an on-stack list, linked through folio->_deferred_list, and deferred_split_scan() takes them off that list with list_del_init() without holding the list_lru lock.
deferred_split_folio() does not know about the on-stack list. It only holds the list_lru lock when it looks at the same list_head, and it can run for such a folio: a THP is queued when it is mapped, as a candidate for the underused check, and is queued "again" when a part of it gets unmapped:
CPU0 deferred_split_scan() CPU1 deferred_split_folio() list_del_init(&folio->_deferred_list) next->prev = prev prev->next = next entry->next = entry list_lru_lock_irqsave() folio_set_partially_mapped() __list_lru_add() list_empty(item) -> true list_add_tail(item, &l->list) item->next = &l->list item->prev = tail entry->prev = entry
The folio now sits on the list_lru with ->prev pointing to itself. The next removal leaves the neighbours pointing to it, and they still do so after the folio has been freed. With CONFIG_DEBUG_LIST:
list_del corruption. prev->next should be ffd4000000270090, but was ffd4000000278090. (prev=ffd4000000270090)
Fix it by grabbing the lock around list_del_init() so deferred_split_folio() cannot race with it.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99725 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt()
cipso_v4_delopt() recomputes the option length by walking the option buffer after the CIPSO option has been moved out. The walk then reads the stale bytes at the tail of the buffer as option data, and a crafted setsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) buffer can make it treat one of them as an option length, increasing opt->opt.optlen beyond the valid option data.
The corrupted length stays on the socket and is later used as the copy length by getsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) and by the udp/raw/ping sendmsg paths, where it exceeds the size of the buffers they copy into.
Compute the new length from the intact options before the move and subtract the CIPSO length, and fill the padding with IPOPT_END.
Score: 7 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99724 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K
On a volume made with "mkntfs -c 8192", a user can set FILE_ATTR_COMPRESSED on an empty file through system.ntfs_attrib. Writing to the file and reading it back after dropping the page cache then crashes:
BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in ntfs_read_compressed_block+0xa2c/0x2040 Read of size 8192 at addr ffff88804355a000 by task dd/106
The read path only handles clusters up to 4K. It copies each cluster out of a single page, and a compression block of 16 8K clusters does not fit in the 64K ntfs_compression_buffer. Loading an inode already rejects compressed data on such volumes.
Reject the flag change the same way.
Score: 7.8 (HIGH) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-99715 [CVSS:3.1 7.5 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
nvme-rdma: fix NULL queue->ctrl dereference on reconnect
Since commit 2a8513091d2f ("nvme-rdma: parallelize I/O queue allocation and startup"), a reconnect that gets more I/O queues than before grows the tag set before the new queues are set up. queue->ctrl is only set by nvme_rdma_setup_io_queues(), so I/O submitted in between reaches nvme_rdma_queue_rq() on a queue that was never allocated and dereferences a NULL queue->ctrl:
BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 000000000000034c RIP: 0010:nvme_rdma_queue_rq+0x52/0xb90

item.title: CVE-2026-99710
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit)
When potentially reusing a shadow page, zap the shadow page if its number of parent PTEs exceeds KVM's (mostly) arbitrary rmap recycling threshold. Letting the guest create a (mostly) unbounded number of parent PTEs allows the guest to coerce KVM into creating lists containing millions of PTEs, effectively bounded only by the maximum number of shadow pages.
Because PTE lists are simple singly linked lists, removal is O(n). Even worse, if a list is constructed just so, teardown can be O(n^2), e.g. if SPTEs are built such that zapping child SPTEs always zaps the last entry in the list. To cap things off, all paths that walk PTE lists do so while holding mmu_lock, without conditionally rescheduling.
Using a doubly linked list would not address the issue, as removal would remain O(n) since KVM still wouldn't know where in the list to remove from. Removal could be made O(1) by storing a per-SPTE pointer, but that would largely defeat the purpose of reusing SPs, and would penalize well-behaved guests, especially for nested TDP where aliasing page tables is uncommon.
So, cap the maximum number of parent PTEs at the rmap limit. In practice, well-behaved guests will likely never run afoul of the limit. E.g. when running Linux as L1 with TDP, the number of parent PTEs for a single SP tops out at under 200 (though undoubtedly obscure workloads can push it higher). Deliberately use a "greater than or equal" as opposed to rmap's strictly "greater than", as the rmap code checks the threshold immediately *after* inserting into the list, i.e. the limit is 1000 for rmaps, KVM just very briefly blows past it.
Apply the check to both indirect and direct SPs, because while a fully direct MMU naturally limits the number of parent PTEs to '1', direct SPs in indirect MMUs have no such constraint. E.g. if the guest maps a huge PTE into many locations in its page tables, and KVM is backing the hugepage with a direct SP, i.e. with a series of smaller pages, then KVM could end up with a direct SP with many parents.
Note, shadow_mmu_try_split_huge_pages() always restarts the rmap walk or bails entirely if it gets to the point where it tries to grab a SP, i.e. there is *no* pre-existing bug that would be tripped by zapping a SP and thus rmaps when getting a SP.

item.title: CVE-2026-99707 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio
collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH. Both paths put back the isolated folio, then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common try_to_unmap_flush().
The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is released. Another collapse can replace and free it. With its PTEs already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs. A CPU can therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio. This has been reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.
Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still held. The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

item.title: CVE-2026-99697 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg
When memory.high is exceeded in non-task context, try_charge_memcg() schedules memcg->high_work without taking a reference on the memcg, and high_work_func() invokes reclaim_high() without pinning the memcg.
With obj_cgroup reparenting, introduced in commit bf4f059954dc ("mm: memcg/slab: obj_cgroup API"), objects charged to a child memcg are reparented to its parent in mem_cgroup_css_offline() instead of holding a reference on the child until uncharged. Subsequent uncharges of those objects go to the parent, which can leave the child's memory use permanently above its high limit, so any later charge on the offlined memcg in non-task context schedules high_work. This was later widened from kernel memory to LRU folios when commit f1cf8d2f36dc ("mm: memcontrol: eliminate the problem of dying memory cgroup for LRU folios") converted LRU folios to use obj_cgroup reparenting.
cancel_work_sync(&memcg->high_work) only runs at the end of teardown in mem_cgroup_css_free(), so high_work_func() can start or still be running reclaim_high() after mem_cgroup_css_released() or shrink_many() has called lru_gen_release_memcg() and unhashed lruvec->lrugen.list. If reclaim tries to rotate the memcg, lru_gen_rotate_memcg() dereferences a NULL pprev pointer. This issue is specific to MGLRU and was introduced with the memcg LRU in commit e4dde56cd208 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: per-node lru_gen_folio lists").
With either traditional LRU or MGLRU, css_free_rwork_fn() calls css_rstat_exit() which frees per-CPU rstat data before calling mem_cgroup_css_free(). If reclaim_high() is still running, rstat updates via mod_lruvec_state() -> __css_rstat_updated() cause a use-after-free on the per-CPU rstat data. This was introduced when commit 5da3bfa029d6 ("cgroup: use separate rstat trees for each subsystem") moved css_rstat_exit() ahead of ss->css_free().

Acquiring the reference in high_work_func() rather than before scheduling high_work is safe because mem_cgroup_css_free() calls irq_work_sync() and cancel_work_sync() which cancels pending work and waits for an already running high_work_func() to complete before mem_cgroup_free() frees the memcg. css_tryget_online() uses percpu_ref_tryget_live() and is safe to call after percpu_ref_exit() before the cgroup is freed unlike css_tryget().

item.title: CVE-2026-99690 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ocfs2: cache the mount context for dentry lock callbacks
ocfs2_drop_dentry_lock() drops the inode reference before releasing the DENTRY lock. This lets inode eviction release the local inode and open locks before a remote unlink can proceed past the DENTRY lock.
A DLM callback can still arrive before the DENTRY lock has been dropped. ocfs2_get_dentry_osb() obtains the mount context through dl_inode->i_sb, which can access a freed inode when the downconvert thread drops the last inode reference in its post-unlock callback:
Downconvert thread DLM callback thread ------------------ ------------------- ocfs2_process_blocked_lock() ocfs2_dentry_post_unlock() ocfs2_dentry_lock_put() ocfs2_drop_dentry_lock() iput(dl->dl_inode) [inode reclaimed after RCU] ocfs2_blocking_ast() ocfs2_get_dentry_osb() dl->dl_inode->i_sb ocfs2_simple_drop_lockres()
Store the mount context in the DENTRY lock resource's l_priv field and use the default mount-context lookup. Recover the containing dentry lock with container_of(), as already done for refcount locks, and remove ocfs2_get_dentry_osb(). ocfs2_dismount_volume() shuts down the DLM before freeing the mount context, so callbacks can use it without accessing the inode. item.title: CVE-2026-99688 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
net/sched: sch_qfq: prevent aggregate self-replacement
qfq_change_class() snapshots the current aggregate settings while holding the qdisc tree lock, but drops the lock before selecting the destination aggregate. During that gap, qfq_enqueue() can move the class to an aggregate matching the requested settings.
When qfq_change_class() resumes, qfq_find_agg() then returns cl->agg. If it is a singleton, qfq_deact_rm_from_agg() frees the aggregate before qfq_add_to_agg() immediately accesses the same pointer, causing a use-after-free.

item.title: CVE-2026-99686 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order
vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nheads[i] but wraps it with a single subtraction. If start + nheads[i] >= 2 * vq->num, start can remain outside the ring.
With used-ring logging enabled, start > vq->num makes (vq->num - start) underflow. log_write() then sets bits beyond the dirty-log bitmap, potentially corrupting adjacent userspace memory. This is reachable on the vhost-net TX path with VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER: done_idx can reach VHOST_NET_BATCH (64), triggering the issue with a 32-entry ring.
Wrap start with a mask to keep it within the ring. VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM enforces a nonzero power-of-two ring size, allowing start to be wrapped using & (vq->num - 1).

item.title: CVE-2026-99685 [CVSS:3.1 8.4 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure

item.description:

item.title: CVE-2026-99674 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices
Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the CAN framework logic and can directly reach a CAN driver's xmit() function. The PF_PACKET framework only checks that skb->len does not exceed the net_device MTU.
For a CAN device that is not CAN XL capable, anything above CANFD_MTU (72 bytes) is therefore dropped before it reaches the driver. However, CAN XL frames are variable length. can_is_canxl_skb() accepts lengths in the range CANXL_HDR_SIZE + CANXL_MIN_DLEN up to CANXL_MTU, i.e. 13 to 2060 bytes.
As a result, an ETH_P_CANXL skb with a length between 13 and 72 bytes can pass both the MTU and the can_dropped_invalid_skb() checks.
A driver that does not support CAN XL will interpret canxl_frame->flags as a length because of the overlap with can_frame->len. And because CANXL_XLF is set, the resulting length is between 128 and 255. For drivers that do not check can_frame->len before copying can_frame->data, as most drivers do, this results in a buffer overflow of up to 247 bytes.
Drop ETH_P_CANXL skbs if the device does not have the CAN_CAP_XL capability. Keep can_is_canxl_skb() for the validation of CAN XL skbs.

item.title: CVE-2026-99672 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock
The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the device's can_ml_priv and travel with the device when it is moved to another network namespace. But they are protected by the per-netns rcvlists_lock. So can_rx_unregister() needs dev_net(dev) to pick the right lock and silently returns when the passed namespace does not match dev_net(dev) anymore.
isotp_release() and bcm_release() leave their notifier list before they take any lock that serializes against the netdev notifier, which runs under RTNL. When the bound device is moved to another namespace in this window, the notifier skips the socket and the release path has to remove the filters itself. isotp_release() passes the socket's namespace, which does not match dev_net(dev) anymore. bcm_rx_unreg() passes dev_net(dev), which can_rx_unregister() reads again for its check, so a namespace change between both reads makes the check fail as well. In both cases can_rx_unregister() silently returns. As can_rx_register() stores rcv->sk without a reference, the remaining receivers point to the freed socket (isotp) or the freed op (bcm):
BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in isotp_rcv+0x1570/0x24d0 Read of size 1 at addr ffff888118130552 by task isotp_ns_uaf/578 can_rcv_filter+0x4af/0x8c0 can_receive+0x28d/0x3c0 can_rcv+0x2a9/0x310 __netif_receive_skb_one_core+0x21a/0x260 process_backlog+0x210/0x760
Besides this, the lists of a device are protected by the rcvlists_lock of the namespace that is passed in. Callers which pass dev_net(dev) read it at different times, so the same lists may be modified under the locks of different namespaces while the device is moved.
Taking RTNL in these release paths is no option: raw_bind(), raw_setsockopt() and raw_release() already hold RTNL while adding and removing up to CAN_RAW_FILTER_MAX filters per socket, which unprivileged users can trigger repeatedly and which makes RTNL a global bottleneck.
Instead fix the root cause and add a spinlock to struct can_dev_rcv_lists, which protects the receive lists of a CAN device or the 'any' CAN device lists of a namespace. It is initialized in can_set_ml_priv(), which is used by all CAN network devices. With this, can_rx_unregister() finds the subscription independently of the current namespace of the device. The protocols keep the device valid with their tracked references. The per-netns rcvlists_lock only protects the receive list statistics anymore, and CAN_RAW, CAN_BCM and CAN_ISOTP pass the namespace that has been used for can_rx_register().
So isotp_release() and bcm_release() now remove their filters correctly without RTNL, and raw_release(), raw_setsockopt(), raw_bind() and isotp_bind() do not need RTNL anymore and add and remove their filters under lock_sock(). To serialize bind() with NETDEV_UNREGISTER, bind() publishes the device inside the RCU section of its lookup, and raw_notify() and isotp_notify() recheck the bound device under lock_sock(). As RTNL does not keep NETDEV_DOWN out of bind() anymore, bind() checks IFF_UP after publishing the bound device, with a barrier pair against raw_notify() and isotp_notify(), so a down transition during bind() is still reported with ENETDOWN.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit
Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bits shift bug") made holebegin and holelen unsigned before they are shifted, by casting them to pgoff_t. That is an unsigned long: on a 32-bit kernel the cast cuts off the upper half of the two loff_t values, so a hole which begins at 4 GiB or beyond is taken for one in the first 4 GiB of the file.
truncate_pagecache() passes the new size of the file and asks for private COWed pages to be unmapped as well. If a file of 6 GiB is truncated to 5 GiB, everything from 1 GiB on is unmapped, and what a process has written to a private mapping of the range between 1 GiB and 5 GiB is lost: it reads the contents of the file again.
Where the range has an end, the wrong range is unmapped instead of the right one. The page cache copes with that, as it unmaps every folio that it removes. The callers which only have unmap_mapping_range() to get rid of user mappings do not, for example drm_vma_node_unmap(), whose fake offsets reach beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit, and revoke_iomem() with physical addresses of more than 32 bits.
Cast to u64 instead. Nothing changes for 64-bit kernels.
Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

item.title: CVE-2026-99650 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in
A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can remain in the swap cache after the process that first mapped it exits. Its anon_vma can then be freed, so ksm_might_need_to_copy() must not dereference it to compare roots.
Doing so can result in some false-positives, resulting in the reverse mapping missing the new folio mapping, preventing migration and reclaim.
SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU allows individual anon_vma objects to be reused immediately after freeing. A stale pointer can then refer to another anon_vma whose root matches, even though the target VMA is not linked to that anon_vma.
Move the anonymous rmap compatibility checks into folio_anon_rmap_compatible(). Keep the page-index check and compare the folio's anon_vma pointer against the VMA's own anon_vma and root first.
If neither matches, bite the bullet and walk the VMA's anon_vma_chain. The VMA keeps these anon_vmas alive, and finding a match guarantees that reverse mapping can find the new mapping.
Lorenzo Stoakes says in a private discussion:
"This isn't quite equivalent to the existing check.
Every anon_vma in an anon_vma_chain shares the same root, but if you split a VMA then fork both of them like this:
VMA A / \ <split> VMA B VMA C \ / root <- anon_vma 1 ----^ ^---- <fork> / parent \ anon_vma 2 anon_vma 3 | | VMA D VMA E
VMA's D and E both get their own new anon_vma's such that:
VMA D: anon_vma 2 -> anon_vma 1 -> root VMA E: anon_vma 3 -> anon_vma 1 -> root
And if you found a folio referencing anon_vma 2, the existing check:
anon_vma->root == vma->anon-vma->root
Would be true for VMA's B, C, D & E.
However after your change it'd be true for VMA D only, as it's the only one with anon_vma 2 in its anon_vma_chain.
Whether or not that could actually happen in practice... 🙂 I don't know.
[...] after your change it'd be true for VMA D only, as it's the only one with anon_vma 2 in its anon_vma_chain. [...] I would [...] say that you are making the test stricter but more correct. "
If this affects performance when KSM was never even involved, we could just track whether KSM ever merged anything and just skip these checks.
There isn't really a lot we can do otherwise: for mapped folios we might be able to use folio_get_anon_vma(), but for unmapped folios there really is no easy way to see if the anon_vma is still valid.
Document the (confusing) lifetime requirements of folio_anon_vma().

item.title: CVE-2026-99645 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use
When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the page might still have a reference from the device. put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new owner while the original holder still references it.
A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists.
Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the pages inside are still in use.
Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak.
While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and switch to pr_warn_ratelimited().
[ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99634 [CVSS:3.1 9.8 CRITICAL]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows
tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child.
MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs.
[ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

item.title: CVE-2026-99633
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/amdgpu: keep the CS user fence BO in GTT
The CS ioctl hands the GPU the GART address of the user fence BO, but since the BO keeps its own preferred and allowed domains, it no longer makes sure the BO is in GTT. A user fence in a VRAM BO, which only needs to be a page in size, gets its address from amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset(), which warns about non-contiguous VRAM. On navi31, a CS with a user fence in a 4K VRAM BO, or in one created with AMDGPU_GEM_CREATE_VM_ALWAYS_VALID:
WARNING: amdgpu_object.c:1531 at amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset+0x86/0xb0 [amdgpu], CPU#11: cs_gem_checks/18393 RIP: 0010:amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset+0x86/0xb0 [amdgpu] Call Trace: <TASK> amdgpu_cs_parser_bos.isra.0+0x4eb/0x850 [amdgpu] amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0x97e/0x2510 [amdgpu] drm_ioctl_kernel+0xac/0x110 [drm] drm_ioctl+0x2c6/0x5b0 [drm] __x64_sys_ioctl+0xa0/0xf0 do_syscall_64+0xa3/0x4d0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e
and BOs which can't be in GTT at all, like GWS or OA ones of a page in size, pass the checks as well.
Only take BOs which can't be anywhere else than in GTT as user fence, which the CS then validates there along with its other BOs. While at it, detect userptrs with amdgpu_ttm_tt_is_userptr(); amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_usermm() returns NULL once the task which created the userptr is gone.

item.title: CVE-2026-99630 [CVSS:3.1 7 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore
An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs") into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated.
The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the running queue.
On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT (debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr:
amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10 amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd) amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000 from client 10
Validate the BOs on the individual needs_update list like before.
(cherry picked from commit eb0d94765d4be18d41e93ad09947dd9cc06ed31a)

item.title: CVE-2026-99628

item.title: CVE-2026-99611 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: line6: Reject capture buffers smaller than two packets
line6_capture_copy() splits the copy into the ALSA ring buffer once at the buffer end and wraps pos_done once, which is only correct when one packet holds at most buffer_size frames. The packet size comes from the device's endpoint, and the per-device hw structs allow 64-byte periods with periods_min 1, so a packet can be larger than the whole buffer. audio_in_callback() logs an oversized packet and then copies it anyway.
The packet size is known at probe time, so constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_BYTES in snd_line6_capture_open() to at least twice the larger of the two endpoints' packet sizes. Two rather than one, because pos_done advances by the packet and wraps once, so a buffer of exactly one packet leaves the position unchanged after every packet. hw_params then rejects a buffer that cannot hold two packets, and the single wrap is valid for every configuration that gets through. Keep a guard in line6_capture_copy() that drops an oversized packet with a ratelimited error, for the case that should no longer be reachable.
Reproduced on 7.3-rc7 with a USB/IP device presenting the GuitarPort interface layout and 1024-byte packets into a 128-byte buffer: ALSA logged "invalid position: pos = 224, buffer size = 32" and the driver logged "driver bug: len" on every following packet. With this patch a 1024-byte buffer is refused at hw_params, and a 2048-byte buffer streams for 30 s with no report and with the position moving inside the buffer.

item.title: CVE-2026-99609 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs
usx2y_urb_capt_retire() wraps the ring buffer once per packet and usx2y_urb_play_prepare() once per URB of nr_of_packs() packets of up to 50 frames. Both assume that the data fits in the buffer, and the hw constraints only require about two 1 ms periods, so a packet larger than the buffer on capture, or a URB larger than the buffer on playback, violates that assumption.
Constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE in snd_usx2y_pcm_open() to at least two URBs, 2 * nr_of_packs() * 50 frames, for both directions. The bound is in frames and derived from the driver's own packet limit, so it does not read the endpoint, whose altsetting is only selected in prepare. Two URBs rather than one, because the position advances by a URB on playback and only moves when a URB is less than the whole buffer. Keep a guard in usx2y_urb_capt_retire() that drops a packet larger than the buffer, for the case the constraint makes unreachable.
With nrpacks above about 163 (S16_LE) or 109 (S24_3LE) the bound exceeds the 64 KiB buffer the substream preallocates (twice that with the preallocation raised to its 128 KiB maximum), so hw_params fails for those module settings. That is intended: the driver cannot be safe with a URB larger than half the largest buffer.
Reproduced on 7.3-rc7 with a USB/IP device presenting the US-122 interface layout and 1024-byte packets into a 512-byte capture buffer:
BUG: KASAN: out-of-bounds in i_usx2y_urb_complete+0x1285/0x1ac0 Read of size 18446744073709551104 at addr ffff88800e448800 by task vhci_rx/83
Tested on 7.3-rc7 with the same device, S16_LE at 44100 Hz, nrpacks 4, so the bound is 400 frames. A 128-frame capture buffer and a 200-frame playback buffer are refused at hw_params with EINVAL. A 400-frame buffer streams for 30 s in each direction with the position advancing inside the buffer and no KASAN report; the capture guard did not fire. The same 400-frame capture buffer with S24_3LE, which selects altsetting 2 in prepare, streams for 30 s with the same result.

item.title: CVE-2026-99603 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners
mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listener directly instead of going through mptcp_listen(). It consequently misses setting SOCK_RCU_FREE on the parent MPTCP socket.
tcp_child_process() can invoke the listener's subflow_data_ready() callback without holding the MPTCP parent lock or a reference to the parent. An authenticated MP_JOIN racing with endpoint teardown can therefore access the parent after its last reference has been dropped. The ADD_ADDR error path can also close an already published listener.
Set SOCK_RCU_FREE before __inet_listen_sk() publishes the TCP listener, matching mptcp_listen(). This protects the parent on every subsequent close path, including a failed endpoint addition.

item.title: CVE-2026-99602 [CVSS:3.1 7.1 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent
udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table extent closest to the goal. It keeps that extent's type and length together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only if goal_elen then reaches zero. UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1 (allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way. For such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the block after the extent, which is in use.
The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use block. Subtracting a block from 0x40000000 then borrows from the type bits, and the extent becomes type 0 with a length of 2^30 - blocksize: about a gigabyte of "free" space overlapping live metadata, the other table extents and whatever lies behind the partition. From then on blocks are handed out twice, or past the end of the partition.
Extents that udf_table_free_blocks() adds are type 0, where the check works, so only tables written by mkudffs or by another implementation are affected. Nothing more than filling such a filesystem is needed: on a fresh 1 MiB "mkudffs --space=unalloctable" image, creating empty files until the partition is full writes file entries over the reserve volume descriptor sequence and the backup anchor, and df then reports a negative amount of used space.
On syzbot's images the same double allocation is what the two reports below trip over. In the first, ftruncate() extends a new file with enough hole extents to need a chain of allocation extent descriptors; one AED is placed on another inode's file entry, and a later one is placed on the block of the AED currently being filled, which udf_setup_indirect_aext() zeroes, so __udf_add_aext() finds lengthAllocDescs out of step with its cursor. In the second, an AED is placed past the end of the device, sb_getblk() fails, and the error path of udf_do_extend_file() calls udf_truncate_extents() on an extent list that no longer covers i_size.
Keep the type separately from the length, as udf_table_prealloc_blocks() already does.

item.title: CVE-2026-99601 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded
udf_table_new_block() hands out the first block of the extent closest to its goal and trusts that the extent covers at least one whole block inside the partition. Nothing checks that. A zero-length extent makes it return the block the extent points at, which need not be free, and the subtraction of one block then underflows the length into the type bits, turning the entry into a bogus continuation. An extent running past the end of the partition makes it return blocks behind the partition.
Such tables are not only found on crafted images: until the previous commit, udf_table_new_block() itself left zero-length extents behind in tables written by mkudffs, and then converted them into extents running past the partition.
Check every extent once when the table is loaded, and refuse read-write access if one is empty, is not a whole number of blocks, or does not lie inside the partition, in the same way as for other allocation information the kernel cannot use. Check first that the table is an Unallocated Space Entry at all: the walk starts at the offset of the allocation descriptors in one, and for a file entry that offset lies before the inode's in-memory copy of the descriptors. Treat a chain of allocation extent descriptors that leads back to itself the same way: the walk would otherwise return the same extents forever, and the mount would never finish. Let a fatal signal interrupt the walk and fail the mount.
Refusing read-write access to an empty extent is deliberate. It shows that an old kernel took the last block but left the entry behind. If consumed again, the entry returns an in-use block and turns into a huge bogus extent. Refusing the table before that happens avoids this second allocation; the filesystem can still be mounted read-only. The check cannot detect every overlap that may already exist in a damaged table.
This patch should be backported together with the previous one: that patch stops creating new empty extents, and this one rejects existing ones before they are consumed again.

item.title: CVE-2026-99597
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
srcu: Add list_splice_init_srcu()
list_splice_init_rcu() makes a list look empty to new readers, waits for the current ones with the given sync function, and only then links the entries into the new list. The sync function takes no argument, so it can wait for RCU readers but not for the readers of an srcu_struct.
Passing synchronize_rcu() for a list read under SRCU still builds, but leaves SRCU readers on the entries while the last one's next pointer is moved onto the new list head. nvme_remove_namespaces() does this today.
Add list_splice_init_srcu(), which waits for the readers of the given srcu_struct instead.

item.title: CVE-2026-99592 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
x86/mm: Fix global ASID handed out to two processes
On AMD CPUs with INVLPGB, two live processes can get the same MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE global ASID value. The two then hit each other's TLB entries, so each can read or corrupt the other's memory.
The global ASID space is managed lazily. When a global ASID is freed, its bit is set in the global_asid_freed bitmap. Once the free ASID search reaches the end of the global_asid_used bitmap, a global flush is done to really reclaim the lazily freed global ASIDs.
However, the current code can assign the same global ASID to two different processes, if one process is assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE - 1, another process MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE, and both stick around (keeping their global ASID numbers in use) until the search wraps around again. At that point a third process could also get assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE.
the highest ASID stays in use, so it is not handed out again last_global_asid stays below it, so no reset the clear bits run out find_next_zero_bit() returns MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE global_asid_available > 0, so the failure is not caught MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE is handed out as an ASID
A search only looks at the bits below MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE, so it cannot see that this value is in use. The next failed search hands it out again, even if the first process still holds it.
The fix used here is to reset the global ASID space after a failed search, and to search again. If that search fails too, no global ASID is handed out.
The test for !global_asid_available is removed, because use_global_asid() only calls allocate_global_asid() if global_asid_available > 0. The remaining test is for a condition that should be impossible.

item.title: CVE-2026-99591 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size
IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (DTE) that is adjacent to the last DTE and falls outside the device table. For example, if the device table can hold 0 to N-1 entries, then the IOMMU can be made to fetch the Nth entry, which falls outside the device table.
The device table is owned by the hypervisor (HV) and is assigned in 4KB pages that are contiguous in system physical address (SPA). If the out-of-bound DTE falls on a guest-owned page, then the guest can exploit this bug to setup malicious table walks to corrupt HV pages and/or bring down the system. Note that this bug does not manifest when the device table size is set to its maximum size of 2MB.
Therefore, force the device table size to the maximum 2MB on affected processors. These are CPU family 0x17 (Zen1/Zen2) through family 0x1a (Zen5/BRH).
This is a mitigation for CVE-2024-21963.
kdump reuses the previous kernel's device table only when the size encoded in the IOMMU device-table register matches pci_seg->dev_table_size. A mixed rollout disagrees: the unpatched kernel uses the IVRS-derived size and the patched kernel uses 2MB, so __reuse_device_table() rejects the table. On SNP-capable IOMMUs that rejection panics the kdump kernel. Kernels that both have this patch agree on 2MB and reuse succeeds. Update the production kernel and the crash kernel together.

item.title: CVE-2026-99589 [CVSS:3.1 8.3 HIGH]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

* batadv_is_my_client() reports the client as not served by this node * batadv_tt_local_client_is_roaming() reroutes unicast frames for it to the node which sent the ROAMING_ADV

item.title: CVE-2026-99586 [CVSS:3.1 8.2 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Handle ARM erratum for CONT under invalidation with SVA
The erratum (MMU-700: #3777127, S3: #3673557) deals with under invalidation of a CONT PTE grouping in the SMMU. The recommended work around is to use a range invalidation that spans the entire CONT. The only user of CONT in the kernel right now is through SVA sharing a CPU page table that contains a CONT created by the mm.
Previously it was thought that this errata was dealt with because the driver always uses range invalidation. However, there is a subtle detail in the errata that the invalidation range must fully enclose the entire CONT for it to work.
It seems that two sequential range invalidations, with a split point falling inside a CONT grouping, will not prevent the errata.
The SMMU's range invalidation generation algorithm does not produce a single invalidation for a single SVA invalidation request, nor does the mm carefully align the SVA invalidation ranges to accommodate the splitting of the invalidation into several ranges.
Thus, when processing a SVA invalidation, the range invalidation splitting routine can generate a range invalidation that is split in the middle of the CONT and risk under invalidation from this errata. This condition could be triggered by a malicious userspace manipulating the TLB gathers via mmap/mprotect/munmap.
Update the errata list to the include the S3 variation, detect the IOMMUs that have it, and then have SVA invalidations use a simplified version of the over invalidation algorithm from the tlbi rework series. This ensures that a single range invalidation is issued for a single MMU notifier callback and now the range invalidation is guarenteed to cover any posible CONT.
Future work to add CONT to iommu_domain page tables should either use this one-invalidate/one-range invalidation algorithm or disable CONT support in the iommu_domain.

item.description:

sctp: hold shkey across socket migration

item.title: CVE-2026-99580 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
mm/userfaultfd: only allocate anon_vma in CoW mappings
find_vma_and_prepare_anon() can end up allocating an anon_vma in VMAs that are not CoW mappings, which is wrong.
If we have a MAP_SHARED R/O file mapped, we lack VM_SHARED (but do have VM_MAYSHARE) and lack VM_MAYWRITE.
While uffd later rejects such mappings (uffd registration requires VM_MAYWRITE, see comment in validate_dst_vma) find_vma_and_prepare_anon() still wrongly allocates an anon vma before it validates the vma.
This in turn later confuses copy_page_range()->vma_needs_copy() such that we end up calling copy_hugetlb_page_range() with ranges that actually do not contain *any* per-pagetable information that would require copying, which is the basis for PMD-table sharing in the first place.
copy_hugetlb_page_range() should not have to worry about shared PMD tables at all: it doesn't make any sense to copy page tables that are shared, as they can be fully recreated later. Ending up in the function with shareable page tables is the real issue.
If a destination PMD table is shared in copy_hugetlb_page_range(), it might get concurrently unshared as we are not holding relevant locks, resulting in us using a page table that is no longer mapped and possibly freed after calling:
dst_pte = huge_pte_alloc(dst, dst_vma, addr, sz);
To fix it, do not allocate an anon_vma in non-CoW mappings and add a safety guard to copy_hugetlb_page_range(), making sure that we never end up messing with shared PMD tables in there.
Before commit 867a43a34ff8a ("userfaultfd: use per-vma locks in userfaultfd operations") we would always validate the VMA before allocating an anon_vma, and consequently never wrongly allocate an anon_vma.
As uffd_lock_vma() is part of the same lookup machinery and also contains a misleading VM_SHARED check, change that one as well directly for consistency.
A follow-up cleanup will stop taking the hugetlb_vma_lock_read(src_vma) lock in copy_hugetlb_page_range() entirely. Further, the usage of VM_SHARED in userfaultfd code should be cleaned up later to focus on CoW vs. non-CoW mappings.

item.title: CVE-2026-99578
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
wifi: rtw88: usb: route bmc frames via the high queue only for DTIM delivery
In AP mode every broadcast and multicast data frame is routed to TX_DESC_QSEL_HIGH, the after-DTIM queue, whether or not anybody is asleep. The firmware drains that queue at beacon pace, a dozen or so frames per second measured on RTL8822BU, while one associated client's mDNS/SSDP chatter alone exceeds that. The excess accumulates inside the chip until the shared TX page pool is exhausted (measured: 14 of 1803 pages left). From that point every host-sourced frame queues behind the backlog: authentication responses reach the air seconds after the client has given up, so no station can associate anymore, and the beacon reserved-page download fails the BCN_VALID poll ("error beacon valid") because it needs pages from the same pool. The AP keeps beaconing, so the failure looks like a silent RX stall and only a reboot recovers.
mac80211 already decides when after-DTIM delivery is needed: it sets IEEE80211_TX_CTL_SEND_AFTER_DTIM on bmc frames only while at least one station is actually dozing. Honor that instead of routing unconditionally: flagged frames keep going through the high queue with the MORE_DATA and HGQMD handling introduced by commit 076f786a0ae1 ("wifi: rtw88: Fix AP mode incorrect DTIM behavior"), everything else leaves at line rate through the AC queues. This partially reverts the usb.c hunk of that commit, whose unconditional routing is what lets the backlog build up.
On a bench AP (USB2, 20 MHz, WPA2, hostapd, a Windows client driven through disconnect/reconnect cycles): reconnects fail 0/5 on RTL8822BU and 0/3 on RTL8821CU before this change, and pass 10/10 and 5/5 with it, with the page pool staying healthy and no beacon errors logged.

item.title: CVE-2026-99577
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
wifi: rtw88: usb: bound what the driver feeds the after-DTIM queue
Frames routed to the high queue are transmitted right after DTIM beacons only, inside the ATIM window, while they wait in the shared TX page pool. The driver puts no limit on how many it hands over, so as long as one station dozes, any sustained broadcast or multicast traffic outruns the drain and empties the pool: measured on an RTL8822BU AP with a single client in power save and ~40 frames/s of mDNS chatter, the free page count at 0x240 goes from 1803 to 16 in about 100 seconds and stays there for as long as the traffic lasts. From that point every other transmit queues behind the backlog, authentication responses arrive too late for anyone to join, and the reserved page download fails ("error beacon valid"). The AP keeps beaconing and only a reboot recovers.
Feed the high queue through a small budget that refills below the measured drain rate (about 3 frames per DTIM, ~15/s at dtim_period 2 on the default 2 TU ATIM window); whatever exceeds the budget leaves on its access category queue right away. The high queue backlog is now bounded by the burst size under any load, so the page pool cannot run dry, at the price that a dozing station may miss part of a broadcast storm.

item.title: CVE-2026-99574 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
f2fs: bound the SIT/NAT bitmaps by the checkpoint pack
sit_ver_bitmap_bytesize and nat_ver_bitmap_bytesize are used as memcpy lengths into and out of sbi->ckpt, which is sized from cp_payload alone, and nothing compares either length against that allocation.
sanity_check_ckpt() has checked these two fields since c77ec61ca0a4, which added them after a crafted image overran build_sit_info(). That check ties each length to a segment count; it never compares either against the allocation, which is the half this adds.
Mounting over-reads in build_sit_info() and build_node_manager(), and the first checkpoint writes the same lengths back through the same pointers, so the over-read's contents reach the on-disk checkpoint. An unmount is enough; the filesystem does not have to be used.
Bound both ends the way __bitmap_ptr() lays them out. The three branches differ, so a single sum of the two lengths would still admit a small overflow when cp_payload is non-zero.

item.title: CVE-2026-99567 [CVSS:3.1 7.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
assoc_array: don't chain a new shortcut onto an existing one
When a full node's leaves and the new key all share the node's segment, assoc_array_insert_into_terminal_node() replaces the node with a shortcut to a pair of new nodes. If the node is itself the target of a shortcut, the new shortcut is installed as that shortcut's next node, and a shortcut leading to a shortcut is something nothing expects: assoc_array_walk() indexes the second one as a node, and assoc_array_apply_edit() hits the BUG_ON() in the loop that adjusts nr_leaves_on_branch, on that same insertion.
Deletion gets a node there. When the subtree below a shortcut shrinks enough, assoc_array_delete() collapses it into one node below the shortcut, and the leaves it collects can all share that node's segment. The next key that shares it too takes this path. Eighteen insertions and a deletion are enough: sixteen keys that agree on bits 0-11, one that leaves them at bit 8 and is deleted again, and one more that agrees with the sixteen.
Have the new shortcut replace the one in front of the node as well. assoc_array_insert_shortcut() gives it that shortcut's back pointer and parent slot, so the caller installs it where that one was, and excises the old shortcut along with the node, which takes a second entry in excised_meta[]. The new shortcut's index key comes from the new key up to the new skip level, so it covers what the old one did.
Found by a userspace test doing random insertions and deletions on keys that share long prefixes; a targeted case builds a shortcut, deletes down to the collapse and inserts one more key.

item.title: CVE-2026-99564 [CVSS:3.1 7.5 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync()
smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() waited for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED after smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work() called rdma_disconnect(). That can take very long, e.g. if the peer just disappeared, until the rdma cm gives up, or forever if the event already happened, but the status was overwritten afterwards.
This is not needed: smbdirect_socket_destroy() drains the qp under rdma_lock_handler(), destroys it and calls rdma_destroy_id(), which only waits for a currently running event handler and makes sure no further events are delivered. The rest of the disconnect protocol (DREQ/DREP and timewait for IB, abrupt close for iWarp) is handled by the rdma core asynchronously. drivers/nvme/host/rdma.c also just calls rdma_disconnect() and ib_drain_qp() before rdma_destroy_id().
So smbdirect_socket_destroy() now also accepts SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTING and changes the status to SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTED itself under rdma_lock_handler().
We could still get RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in the small windows between rdma_unlock_handler() and rdma_destroy_id(), but in that case smbdirect_connection_rdma_event_handler() is basically a no-op.

item.title: CVE-2026-99563 [CVSS:3.1 7.5 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener
A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was destroyed. So every connection that failed before it was accepted (negotiate timeout, peer disconnect, invalid negotiate request, ...) stayed on the list and counted against the backlog until the listener was destroyed. After about backlog (10 for ksmbd) such connections smbdirect_listen_connect_request() rejected every new connection with -EBUSY, so an unauthenticated peer was able to permanently stop ksmbd from accepting SMB-Direct connections.
Now a failed child moves itself to a new listen.orphaned list at the end of smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work(), after the disconnect was started, and queues listen.purge_orphaned_work, which releases it with smbdirect_socket_release(), without holding the listener's rdma_lock_handler() lock, in the same way smbdirect_socket_destroy() does for the remaining children. Orphaned sockets still count against the backlog until they are released.
sc->accept.listener is now only changed under listener->listen.lock and whoever clears it is responsible for releasing the socket: smbdirect_socket_accept(), purge_orphaned_work or the destroy of the listener.
In order to make that work:
- a struct smbdirect_socket that is a listener is now freed via kfree_rcu(), so that a child can dereference sc->accept.listener under rcu_read_lock(), even if the listener is released concurrently.
- smbdirect_listen_connect_request() adds nsc to the listen.pending list and sets nsc->accept.listener before it calls smbdirect_accept_connect_request(), and always returns 0 so the rdma_cm core keeps the connection id and nsc owns it. On a non-zero return it schedules nsc's teardown with smbdirect_socket_schedule_cleanup(), which orphans it off the listener so that purge_orphaned_work releases it; nsc destroys its own connection id with rdma_destroy_id() in that teardown. The teardown has to be deferred because the rdma_cm core holds nsc's id_priv->handler_mutex across the handler, so nsc->rdma.cm_id must not be destroyed synchronously from here. That same handler_mutex (and the listener's) also guarantees nsc can't go away under us, so setting the listener before the call is safe and lets a failure orphan nsc.
- smbdirect_accept_negotiate_recv_work() no longer moves a socket to the ready list if it already failed or no longer belongs to the listener. Every accepting socket has a listener, so if sc->accept.listener is already cleared, it no longer sends a negotiate response, as the socket is about to be released.
- smbdirect_socket_destroy() of the listener disables purge_orphaned_work and also releases the orphaned sockets.

item.title: CVE-2026-99556 [CVSS:3.1 8.8 HIGH]
item.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir
SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it calls iterate_dir() on fp->filp. An SMB2 SET_INFO request with FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION can resolve the same FileId and call ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir() on the same filp without that lock.
iterate_dir()'s inode read lock permits concurrent readers and does not serialize per-file iterator state. ext4 stores its dx readdir cursor and fname RB tree in file->private_data. Concurrent reset or refill can therefore free a fname node while the other worker still traverses it or retains its RB-tree link, resulting in use-after-free accesses.
An authenticated SMB client with list and delete rights on a directory in a writable KSMBD share backed by ext4 can trigger this when the directory takes the dx readdir path. The client overlaps an SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY request with an SMB2 SET_INFO request carrying FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION on one live FileId.
In one x86_64 SMP KASAN multi-shot guest using ksmbd-for-next at 171df27077fb, the unmodified kernel reported a cross-worker use-after-free before a panic. The first report's access and free stacks show the two request paths directly (trimmed):
BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550 Read of size 8 by task kworker/2:0/29 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work Call Trace: ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550 htree_dirblock_to_tree+0x535/0x990 ext4_htree_fill_tree+0x319/0xba0 ext4_readdir+0x175a/0x2f40 iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630 smb2_query_dir+0x1003/0x1cc0
Freed by task 279: free_rb_tree_fname+0x67/0xc0 ext4_readdir+0x13a9/0x2f40 iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630 ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir+0xa2/0x100 smb2_set_info+0x2ffa/0x45d0
Take fp->readdir_lock across the entire emptiness check. This places both iterators over that handle's filp in the same lock domain while preserving the disposition status handling. The exact code change completed a warning-free x86_64 KASAN bzImage build. Tracing three request pairs showed that the two iterate_dir() calls no longer overlapped and the expected statuses were preserved. A further 1,600 reproducer iterations completed with expected statuses and no KASAN report, Oops, or panic.
The reproducer and complete guest configuration are available privately to maintainers on request.
